summary: Evidence packet for the runx postmortem-maker skill (automerchlab/postmortem-maker@2.0.1). The skill reads a real incident thread over HTTPS at run time, reconstructs a cited timeline, refuses to invent a root cause, and — only when the cause is confirmed — executes the publication through the package's own provider adapter and then reads the delivered message back out of the outbox and re-digests it. The dogfood below runs the PUBLISHED package against a live GitHub incident thread: run 1 executes the delivery, run 2 re-runs the same incident and gets the original delivery back as an idempotent replay (proving the first delivery is durable and is consumed by a later run), and the withheld path is covered by the harness with explicit no-delivery assertions.

output.root_cause_statement: #3722 is named as the cause in an unhedged statement in the incident thread

send_plan_approval.reason: root cause confirmed against cited thread evidence

delivery_result.transport: bundled append-only outbox log (not a hosted provider)

readback.verified_independently: re-read from the outbox file and re-digested; not copied from the deliver step output

replay_run.detail: the second run over the same incident returns the delivery made by run 1 instead of sending again, and the outbox stays at one message — the first delivery is durable and is read back by a later, separate run of the published package

withheld_run.result: refused (exit 1): no timeline could be reconstructed from that thread
withheld_run.detail: a live run against a thread that does not settle its own cause delivered nothing; the outbox still holds exactly the one message from run 1. The full withheld path — unknowns recorded, publication withheld, and the explicit no-delivery assertions (send_plan_created=false, provider_act_performed=false, delivery_exists=false, outbox_unchanged=true) — is exercised by the conflicting-evidence-withheld harness case

observations.value: provider=bundled-local-outbox: an append-only outbox log bundled with the package, not a hosted provider and not the runx data-store. Canonical runx/send-as is a planning layer that never delivers, and native data.* tools are not in the execution closure of a registry-installed package, so the package ships its own adapter with compare-and-set, idempotency and readback.
observations.detail: Stated plainly so nothing in this packet reads as a claim that a hosted provider delivered anything.
